generator.params.basal_area.note: The area its `basal` look draws on an organ 1 m long (plantc atlas, 2026-10-17), so it shades with what it shows: Berberidaceae's spiny margin now cuts its leaflets' teeth, where before it drew the generic simple card (0.235).

generator.params.bud_area.note: The leaf area its `bud` look draws on an organ 1 m long (plantc's shading-area test), so it shades with what it shows: the bud is now its flower closed, where before it drew the fruit ovoid.

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944), as Mahonia nervosa, Fig. 1867, p. 217: simple stems 2 dm to 6 dm high with the leaves in a terminal tuft.

appearance.organs.flower.shape.petal_who.note: Jepson's Manual (1925), Berberidaceae: sepals 6, in 2 circles; petals 6, in 2 circles; stamens as many and opposite them. So six petals, three and three.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a low evergreen shrub of a few short stems, each topped by a rosette of long pinnate leaves with holly-like, spiny leaflets and upright racemes of yellow flowers. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 0.5 m tall at 6 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: dark, slightly glossy green leaflets; yellow flowers; blue berries. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): six yellow petals and six sepals by hand (both in two whorls of three, as Jepson's Manual of 1925 gives the family), six stamens and one pistil, from the characters of Berberidaceae by the rules at the flowering plants.

taxon.note: Common name (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

generator.program.note: Its family's herb program, though it grows as a low shrub: Berberis spans two forms, so the species names its own (growth plan G2.3a).

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

taxon.scientific_name.note: WCVP v16's accepted name for the plant the spec's authors wrote as Mahonia nervosa, which WCVP treats as a synonym.

taxon.genus.note: The genus WCVP v16's accepted name is written in.
